title: My worms spinoff of proRoper - Whiplash
author: whiplash-dev
selftext:
[playwhiplash.dev](http://playwhiplash.dev)

You can actually play a demo version online now.  Like the full thing. im just an indie game dev, so i pretty much push everything to the main website, cause who's got time to make a real demo? 

Completely vibe coded.  Been tweaking for 2 months or so.  Continuously adding new features to make it more fun and to look better. Recently redid the entirety of the lighting using some free Fable credits.

Opus 5.5 for the win.

it is a few versions behind though.....i think the multiplayer still works.  
  
give....me....feedback...PLZZ

\---

a platformer where you use a rope and swing.  Again, based of worms armageddon's ninja rope.  

There IS platform destruction, but its pretty much off by default and only in specific areas.  

Modes:

1. Reach the exit  
2. Collect Relics  
3. Destroy targets  
4. Race  
5. Multiplayer (collect a relic, attack, hide)  
6. Time Attack (collect as many relics as you can, and get some time ups to push further).

Do I have something here or not?

comments.author: challengethegods
comments.body:
worms ninja rope shenanigans were always so much fun and very often created comical failures. I think the massive value of worms was the way it operated on the edge of catastrophe all the time, so even if I was better than my brother/friends at playing it there was always a chance I blow myself up in some silly way trying to be fancy with the ninja ropes and grenades. 

for this game, I'd personally focus on improving the controls and character - try to make them more of a ninja with rope on the side rather than a snail that happens to abuse the rope to go 500mph. I'd prefer to start the game running and jump/dash/tumble/etc even before relying on the rope.  N++ with a ninja rope sounds awesome, but ninja rope snail makes it feel like a gimmick.  The other thing I see here is how the 1/2/3/4 keys are awkward, click and space are redundantly doing the same thing instead of a much more intuitive space to jump, ninja rope is always straight up until it isn't, instead of being a ninja and aiming at the cursor while jumping and double jumping and wall sliding and stuff. There is so much room here to go higher, really, but it looks like a better more fun character might dominate the level design that was already in place, so I'm not sure how appealing this advice sounds.  
  
aside from that, the game seems to either be slow to download/stream(?), or very poorly optimized. A game like this should have 100ms loading screens. My entire game's startup time is 100ms and it has 100+ gigantic startup phases across thousands of components. Sitting here on my badass computer watching a 10sec loading screen for a single level of an SNES kind of game is a bad look. If you're looking for easy wins where you can change something and have the result be "objectively better" with no pro/con hesitations wondering if it's the right way to go, then optimization is the perfect thing to work on next. 

there is also some glaring vibe coded tone to all the UI/text/details so make sure each individual component/label/etc is something you wanted to put there rather than the AI filling in placeholders that you glance across as being good enough (especially true when it starts deciding random hotkeys or labeling them in the UI and putting little mini-tutorials about its weird control scheme everywhere and stuff like that)  

hope it doesn't sound like too much critique but I think fixating on these problems is the best way to refine/iterate this game in its current state

replies.author: whiplash-dev
replies.body:
truly appreciate the feedback.  youre amazing dude.

it actually would load faster if the levels weren't directly editable and destructible.   Currently, if a level is created in the editor - in order to keep it so you can continually edit the level - it applies the texture, light and shader details during the load.  So essentially its 'rendering' the map each time you go into it.  This is by design - but can be improved im sure, especially for campaign maps.  

it is \~not\~ very well optimized at the moment, i agree - especially on web.  though a nice computer can power through it.

still heavy in the alpha phase, all the assets are just "good enough" - they're all likely going to go through a real upgrade phase at some point.  

\---

As far as your feedback on the gameplay - the ninja rope is supposed to fire at the direct opposite angle you were previously hanging at.  I made it shoot straight up if you spin or turn around - to allow you to regain some positioning.  I got so used to it - i like it.  But i can understand if its jarring - definitely good feedback.

I do like the slow wobbling worminess.  But i did add phase dash thing - where you shoot across the screen - and can continue to add some additional movement options.  

Good info to think about, I might try speeding him up a bit and seeing how it moves. 

thanks again for all the feedback, everything is noted, and will certainly impact what i do moving forward.

replies.author: challengethegods
replies.body:
the aesthetic here and its overall vibe are really good, and the general direction of the ninja theme is also great. I think I would lean into that even more - what you have now feels a lot like a ninja-adjacent parkour 'realism', but if you can push it to a higher level without going as far as completely supernatural mobility it would probably have a way more compelling baseline to build around. Same as the other advice, I could definitely understand any kind of foundation level changes feeling like they table flip existing level designs and balance, but a few things I noticed that drag it down are lack of sprint/dash style \[shift\] controls, and lack of a double jump (which could even be a half-jump flip in the air or something, not literal jumping on air), and some kind of tumble-into-roll on landing if you have horizontal speed.   
  
Something I have noticed in my past projects is that the baseline character mobility controls and their variety is 90% of the game's "skill expression", while everything outside of the character like levels/enemies/goals/etc are just opportunities to express that skill. As a random example, I have a first person shooter project with warframe ninja mobility and grapple hooks, but it also has fall damage. There is also sneak on \[ctrl\], but if you have some horizontal motion and hold ctrl as you are landing you will flip/tumble and eliminate the fall damage. Essentially this means the game could just skip over that and remove all fall damage in terms of its raw 'RPG balance', but while playing it and deliberately pressing the key to tumble it feels like you're more of a badass, compared to the game just handing that to you. One caveat is that shift/ctrl/alt start to get weird inside a browser and trigger hotkeys and stuff, so I am not suggesting the ctrl-tumble as much as using it as an example of the way these subtle control scheme details can affect how high the skill ceiling feels in the gameplay. Some similar things that stack onto existing keys are having the time spent holding a key affect its magnitude slightly (ex: hold jump longer = slightly longer jump / hold grapple hook longer = slightly longer hook shot length), and a good north star for mobility is to create some theoretical momentum transfer path between every mode of mobility so that they can intuitively transition and mix/match everything together without abruptly losing their pacing (for this, only the deepest vertical 'fall damage' style impacts should stifle them). The rope mechanic itself may also need more fine tuning and calibration - try to require a bit more momentum of swinging, but not so much that it becomes tedious.

I think character/mobility is by far the strongest axis of influence to determine what the game is here, so I focus on that, but there are some little nitpicks and random details in the entry barrier as well. It seems if you're in a kind of half-attention flow you will replay the first level 3 times in a row, the emphasis on retry is very strong while selecting a new level is relegated into a secondary consideration. I also wonder if a casual gamer would find the first stage too hard to learn in, but I'm not sure what would be better. The risk here is that there is a pit to fall into and if they are not getting it they could get frustrated trying to reach the exit. I wonder if something like a no-brainer tunnel environment or one where the exit is on the ground and the crystals are the harder part would be a good idea here. The genius of N/N++ games is how the coins are like a stretch goal, with some of the coins being insanely hard to get, but level difficulty is at a baseline of simply reaching the exit.

I would keep working on this, it's very promising, good job.

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body: Amazing feedback and I really like everything you brought up. You’re right that I’ve ignored mobility beyond swinging, so there’s a lot to explore there.   I agree also about the first map. I should make it just a straight cavern with no chance of getting stuck or learning any verticality. I’m putting your comment in my feedback folder for future updates. Thank you very much for taking a moment to play and provide feedback 💜
